# Real-User Authenticity Standard

This policy is mandatory for every agent and every workflow that evaluates,
demonstrates, or makes a claim about the product's user experience.

## The hard rule

A user-facing capability is proven only through the real application, a genuine
account, the account's real persisted state, and the real service path that a
customer uses.

Agents must never use any of the following in live-user, browser, end-to-end,
release-acceptance, demo-readiness, or production-validation work:

- Network or API mocks, route interception, stubbed service responses, fabricated
  success payloads, or fake generated assets.
- Seeded or preloaded product data that did not enter through the visible user
  workflow during the current account journey.
- Bypassed, injected, pre-authenticated, impersonated, or simulated
  authentication state.
- Artificial subscription, quota, entitlement, usage, organization, plan, or
  tier mutation.
- Hidden database, local-storage, API, console, or source-code manipulation that
  places the product into a state the user did not reach through the UI.

For free-user validation, create a genuinely new free account and discover the
real limits presented to that account. Never convert an account to “free” by
changing state behind the UI.

## Credential and environment rule

Use `https://indii.music/` for production real-user validation unless the user
explicitly requests another deployed environment. A local build is not
production evidence.

If a genuine signup or sign-in requires an email link, OTP, CAPTCHA, credential,
or authorization that the agent does not have, stop at that point and request
the official user authorization flow. Never replace missing credentials with a
fixture, token injection, alternate identity, or adjacent authentication
mechanism.

## Evidence and verdicts

A `PASS` requires evidence from the real UI and, where relevant, a reload,
sign-out/sign-in, or downstream reuse that proves the state persisted normally.
Capture the visible result and record the exact account tier and environment.

If the real path cannot be completed, the honest verdict is `BLOCKED`,
`UNAVAILABLE`, or `FAIL` with the observed reason. A simulated success is always
a failure of the testing process.

## Existing automated tests

The repository contains legacy unit, component, and browser suites that use
test doubles or simulated state. They may remain as isolated structural
regression checks until separately migrated, but:

- Agents must not run or cite a mock-backed suite as real-user, end-to-end,
  release, production, or free-tier evidence.
- Agents must not add or expand mocks for a user journey, external service,
  authentication path, persisted customer state, or plan/entitlement behavior.
- When an agent touches a mock-backed user-path test, it must either migrate the
  path to genuine integration or clearly classify the remaining test as
  structural-only and leave the real-user claim unverified.
- Deterministic unit tests may use literal inputs for pure logic, but those
  inputs must not impersonate a customer, external service, authenticated
  session, persisted product history, or paid/free entitlement.

CI may continue to execute legacy structural suites during migration. A green
legacy suite does not override a failed or unverified real-user path.

## Reporting language

Every agent report that discusses user-facing validation must state:

1. The real environment used.
2. Whether the account was genuinely created through the UI.
3. The actual plan shown by the product.
4. Whether any part of the path remains blocked or unverified.

Never use “real user,” “end-to-end,” “production verified,” “free-tier verified,”
or equivalent language when any part of the claimed path used simulation.

### ISSUE-1691: Five e2e specs fail on main and turn every PR red

- **Status:** 🟡 PARTIAL — Detroit Techno and the two earlier specs repaired (Detroit passed CI on #982 head dfc41290); the MCP path awaits an owner-run @live pass on indii.music
- **Severity:** 🟠 HIGH
- **Module:** e2e / CI
- **Evidence:** base run actions/runs/44874990405 (shard 2: detroit-techno-onboarding:120, distribution-workflow:178, indii-macro-flywheel:61; shard 3: mcp-a2a-routing:22, mcp-boardroom-collaboration:22).
- **Findings so far:**
  - indii-macro-flywheel: real app-support bug. `FirestoreService` e2e mock mode emitted `subscribe` once on mount and never again, so a campaign created afterwards never appeared. Fixed by notifying open subscribers on every mock write (`FirestoreService.e2eSubscribe.test.ts`). The spec's original strict assertion now passes unchanged.
  - distribution-workflow: spec drift from ISSUE-969, which requires a real hashed master and a staged cover before a release can submit. The mocked suite has neither, so the test now verifies the gate (submit disabled, missing-asset message) instead of delivery. Full submission still needs a genuine account with an ingested master and remains unverified.
- **Impact:** every PR is red on the same specs, hiding real regressions.
- **Acceptance:** all five specs pass in CI, or carry a skip that names the missing service and is recorded here.
- **Root causes of the last three specs (2026-11-21, verified by local runs with `VITE_FIREBASE_PROJECT_ID=mock-project`):**
  - detroit-techno-onboarding, **real app bug:** onboarding stayed interactive while the store still held the blank placeholder profile (no uid) left by the account-boundary reset. The career path and answers were written onto that placeholder, then the user's real profile load landed about 20s later and replaced them, so the "Choose Your Career Path" picker came back mid-chat. The spec's non-exact "Touring" click then hit the picker's "Touring Band" card, which is why the earlier exact-match attempts could never pass. Fixed in two layers: `OnboardingPage` shows "Loading your profile…" with Retry until the profile has a uid (`OnboardingPage.test.tsx` "Profile readiness"), and `loadUserProfile` keeps local edits newer than the stored copy, the same rule its live listener already used (`profileSlice.test.ts`).
  - detroit-techno-onboarding, **spec drift (4 items):** the finished cover now opens the full-screen canvas editor over the sidebar (close it first); release submit is gated by ISSUE-969 (assert the gate, as distribution-workflow does); QC title/artist moved to the Metadata sub-tab; Finance tabs are grouped (ISSUE-1440). The spec also seeded its profile before the app's own reset and load had settled; it now waits for the loaded uid and seeds with a current `updatedAt`. Persona 2's "Vintage" style and turn-3 options are now values from `OPTION_WHITELISTS.aesthetic_style`.
  - mcp-a2a-routing and mcp-boardroom-collaboration: the 2026-11-19 root cause was right; an earlier 2026-11-21 note here (now replaced) wrongly said these specs did NOT need a real MCP server. `SSEClientTransport` reads tool results from the long-lived SSE stream, which `route.fulfill` closes at once. Fixed with a real local SSE gateway, `e2e/fixtures/mcpSseServer.ts` (same `SSEServerTransport` as `packages/firebase/src/mcp/index.ts`) on the dev endpoint `127.0.0.1:5001`. The auth fixture's Cloud Functions catch-all also matched `:5001`, so each spec lets `**/mcpEndpoint/**` through. The old assertion expected the raw tool payload in chat, but the app marks tool payloads system-only; the specs now assert that the gateway received the call (with the user's arguments) and that the Publicist's message reports "Executed remote tool: generate_playlist_pitch". No seat answers as `manager`; the Conductor (`generalist`) posts the coordination summary.
- **Repair evidence:** local runs: detroit-techno-onboarding 1 passed (4.6m, all 5 personas); mcp-a2a-routing + mcp-boardroom-collaboration 2 passed (29.6s); vitest onboarding/profile/marketing 132 passed. Mock-backed, so structural only (`.agent/REAL_USER_AUTHENTICITY.md`): a real slow-network onboarding run on a genuine account has not been done.
- **MCP stub withdrawn (2026-11-21):** Codex P1 on #982: the local SSE stub (`e2e/fixtures/mcpSseServer.ts`) is a new fake external service, which `.agent/REAL_USER_AUTHENTICITY.md` forbids. It is removed. A genuine run can't happen in CI: the gateway fails closed without a real Arcjet key, needs a verified real account and a release the caller owns, and `generate_playlist_pitch` makes a paid Vertex call; emulators would still need seeded users and an injected token. The two legacy specs are now tagged `@external-legacy @structural` (excluded from `npm run test:e2e`), and the genuine check is `e2e/mcp-publicist-live.spec.ts` (`@live`, sign-in through the visible UI, no mocks). It needs `PLAYWRIGHT_BASE_URL=https://indii.music`, `PRODUCTION_SHA`, `E2E_TEST_EMAIL`/`E2E_TEST_PASSWORD` and `E2E_LIVE_RELEASE_ID`, so only the owner can run it. Closure needs that live pass.
- **Local run tips:** the installed Chromium is build 1243, so use a throwaway config outside git that sets `executablePath: '/opt/pw-browsers/chromium'`, `video: 'off'` and `screenshot: 'off'` (no ffmpeg). Do not run two Playwright jobs at once; they share the dev server on port 4242 and one can kill it.

# Current live-user testing protocol

Updated October 4, 2026. This is the operating protocol for future live sessions. It supersedes stale starting-state and standby instructions in the original Real Artist Program. The four artist dossiers remain scenario sources; historical audits remain historical evidence.

## Core purpose

Act like a working artist using https://indii.music to accomplish useful work. Evaluate what the artist expects, what each control actually does, when the app should act, and whether the result is usable. Clicking a button or receiving an agent assurance is not proof of completion.

This update prepares the next session; it does not claim that the current deployment has been tested.

## Start with the app that exists now

At the start of each run, inspect the visible app and record its current navigation, available tools, account, project, displayed plan, and version if shown. Inventory available source files and existing records without changing them. Do not reuse August account, quota, asset-count, tab-name, model, or credential assumptions.

Use the existing authorized founder account when available. Record its actual privileges; founder access cannot prove a free customer's experience. A separate free-tier claim requires a genuine free account reached through normal signup. If authorization expires, stop that path and present the official sign-in flow.

Documentation supplies expectations and questions, not proof. Distinguish a shipped feature, a proposal, an account restriction, and an unavailable platform feature. Reconcile contradictory descriptions against visible behavior and record any unresolved expectation.

## Four reusable artist journeys

| Artist | Useful session objective | Connected outcomes to check |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Mara June / Porchlight | Prepare and reconcile a small café show | Booking details, $120 income, travel clarification, strings receipt, expenses, quick road note, promotional draft |
| Signal Bloom / Afterhours | Prepare a techno release and club promotion | Master and stems ingestion, audio analysis, suitable visual direction, image/video edits, release metadata, campaign draft, travel |
| Northbound Static / Bandstand | Prepare a Flint band release or regional show | Member credits and splits, shared expenses, gear, tour book, master audio, campaign assets, release package; later rights changes |
| Nia Rook / Cipher | Prepare a Rust Belt battle appearance or mixtape | Beat provenance and rights, travel, receipts, lyrics/metadata, portrait-led promo, release preparation, opportunity notes |

Use these as consistent character contexts, selecting tasks supported by today's app. Keep fictional career events explicitly fictional. Do not manufacture years of persisted history. In the founder account, keep persona work in clearly identified projects where the UI supports it; do not overwrite the user's identity.

## How to execute a task

1. State a natural artist goal and a concrete expected result.
2. Reach the tool through normal navigation and use realistic inputs, including conversational corrections and imperfect notes.
3. Observe the action, visible feedback, timing, resulting object, and next available step.
4. Open or use the output. Check that it reflects the inputs and selected settings.
5. Navigate away and return; reload when appropriate to confirm saved state.
6. Reuse the result in a connected department or workflow and verify that the correct information follows it.
7. End with delivered value, an explained limit, an authorization requirement, an unavailable capability, or an evidence-backed defect.

Explore different tasks and combinations. Repeat a test when needed to reproduce a failure, verify a repair, or compare a fixed benchmark. Avoid endless clicks that do not advance an artist goal.

## Interaction and visual checks

For every reachable button, swatch, menu, tab, toggle, slider, upload, keyboard action, and dialog encountered, check its meaning, prerequisite, response, and recovery path. A selected control should affect the next relevant action or explain why it cannot. Cancel should cancel; save should persist; download should yield a usable file; undo should restore the intended prior state.

Check empty, selected, loading, success, failure, and return states where reachable. Look for clipped bottom controls, unnecessary nested scrolling, overlapping panels/toasts, confusing duplicate actions, unreadable text, lost drafts, and difficult navigation between departments. Multiple access points are acceptable when their context makes sense. Desktop resizing is not proof of native mobile or Electron behavior.

No additional screenshots are requested. Use visible text, browser observations, and existing evidence; record viewport dimensions for layout findings when available.

## Priority connected workflows

- **Images:** Use the authorized real selfies and suitable existing assets. Test upload/open, selection, drawing, text/shapes, color swatches, layers, crop, undo/redo, save/reopen, variants, and export wherever supported. For regional editing, mark the turntable green and mixer orange, request a white turntable and orange mixer, then inspect both changed regions and preservation of the remainder. Merely changing swatch selection does not prove the edit.
- **Video:** Test source upload/playback, references and first/last frames, shot controls, timeline operations, edits, preview, save/reopen, and export wherever the current UI supports them. Verify actual duration, framing, audio, and output quality rather than trusting setting labels. Distinguish generation, editing, assembly, and export.
- **Audio intelligence:** Ingest an actual available track, observe processing status and analysis, and ask Creative to use that track's musical information for visual direction. Check correct track attribution and downstream retrieval. Genre-appropriate prose alone does not prove audio analysis was consulted. Missing analysis should trigger an actionable next step, not invented tempo/key facts.
- **Agent collaboration:** Ask the current department manager for useful work, and test the coordinator/Boardroom route for a task crossing departments. Creative should perform authorized creative work; Finance should request Creative assistance for a financial visual. Check manager-to-manager coordination, department employee boundaries, retained context, actual tool outcomes, and absence of duplicate actions. A planning-only request proves planning only.
- **Distribution/DDEX:** Follow source audio, artwork, credits, identifiers, ownership/splits, release metadata, validation, package preparation, correction, and downstream reuse through the UI. Inspect exported packages when available. Package creation does not prove distributor delivery or acceptance. Stop before unapproved external transmission.
- **Artist operations:** Test documents/receipts/notes ingestion, clarification, financial records, bookings, tour-book layout, campaign drafts, social account settings, and correction propagation. Confirm estimates and missing evidence remain distinguishable from confirmed facts.

## Authenticity and authorization

Read the repository's .agent/REAL_USER_AUTHENTICITY.md before live testing. Fictional source documents and music are allowed; mocked responses, injected authentication, seeded product state, hidden state changes, and artificial entitlements are not. Enter source material through the normal user interface.

Existing session authorization covers ordinary in-app testing and reversible drafts. Respect the user's existing boundaries for purchases, upgrades, paid generation, public posts, distributor transmission, outreach, credential changes, and destructive changes to real work. Record any path blocked by those boundaries precisely; do not call it a product failure. Do not introduce extra approval steps for ordinary authorized work.

## Findings and repair handoff

### Product data authenticity sweep

Across every department, inspect metrics, charts, transactions, contacts, bookings, catalog entries, notifications, recommendations, activity feeds, and agent claims for app-supplied mock or invented data. User-uploaded fictional test sources remain permitted; the app must not substitute fabricated records or service results.

For displayed data, seek its source through normal detail views: account/project ownership, underlying record, date, source file or integration, processing receipt, and normal persistence. Missing provenance is UNVERIFIED, not automatic proof of a mock. Confirmed app-supplied mock data requires a repair annotation to connect the feature to its real authoritative database/service. Until connected, show an honest empty, unavailable, or setup-required state rather than invented values. A database connection alone is insufficient if its records were automatically seeded as fake customer history.

Use browser evidence first. A repair agent may trace the data source in code, but the live tester must verify the corrected customer path afterward. Do not delete suspicious records merely because their origin is unclear.

Record: date/run, environment, account provenance, displayed tier, persona/project, goal, starting state, exact actions, expected result and its basis, actual result, visible evidence, timing, persistence/downstream checks, impact, and verdict.

Use PASS, FAIL, BLOCKED, UNAVAILABLE, or UNVERIFIED. Separate observed facts from suspected causes. For ambiguous behavior, allow loading to settle, check the actual target, retry once if safe, and try a natural alternative. An inaccessible automation selector is not automatically a broken user control. A gallery card can be clickable without a nested button. Absence of a visible cost panel alone does not prove a billing or approval bypass.

Each confirmed failure receives a **Repair annotation** with reproduction, expected behavior, evidence, impact, and a concrete retest. The testing operator records and verifies; the repair agent implements. Do not invent root causes or mark an issue fixed from code/CI alone. Recheck historical findings against today's deployment and mark them reproduced, resolved, changed, or unverified without erasing the original record.

content.text:
I stopped before uploading anything, because even a complete release wouldn't let this test pass. The files aren't the problem; I have them: the master would be `Desktop/indii.music.demo.music/05 wiil - Owner Testing/Assembly Line Halo.wav`. The app itself blocks the path in two places, both found in the source on main:

1. **Releases are saved where the Publicist's tool doesn't look.** The Distribution screen saves releases in one database collection (`proprietaryIngestionReleases`). `generate_playlist_pitch` only accepts a release id from two other collections (`users/{uid}/releases` or `releases`). Nothing in the app, the Cloud Functions or the desktop code creates records in either of those two. So any id from Distribution would be rejected with "Forbidden: release not found or not owned by caller". See `packages/firebase/src/mcp/helpers.ts:43` and `packages/renderer/src/services/distribution/DistributionSyncService.ts:62`.
2. **Submitting a release on the web stops partway.** `DistributionService.submitRelease` throws "Electron environment required for release submission", so app.indii.music can't finish creating a release. Before that error, the form has already saved the cover and written a "cover_art_audit_pending" record, which would leave a half-finished release on your account.

Separately, the built-in browser can't attach files from my side. I would have had to use Claude in Chrome for the uploads.

Nothing was uploaded, created or sent, and no AI call was made. ISSUE-1691 is unchanged.

What I'd do next:
- Record this run on ISSUE-1691 as 🟡 PARTIAL, blocked, with the build SHA (`c1f2c2ae6`) and the time.
- Log the collection mismatch as a new issue, and mark ISSUE-1691 as depending on it.
- Open a PR from a branch off origin/main.

The other choice is to try it live anyway: upload through Chrome, which leaves a half-finished release record on your account, and capture the real Forbidden response. That run's Boardroom turn would still make the AI call you approved.

Should I log it as blocked with the new issue and open the PR, or try it live anyway?
Yes, log and PR

### ISSUE-1158: Generated-audio library service writes to an unruled path while rules authorize a different collection

- **Playback object-identity repair (2026-11-14):** Shared `resolveStorageUrl` now passes the full persisted `gs://` URI to Firebase `ref`, retaining its bucket instead of resolving the path in the default bucket. This matches [Firebase reference construction](https://firebase.google.com/docs/storage/web/download-files#create_a_reference). A local installed-SDK construction check confirmed that an explicit bucket survives a different default-bucket configuration; it made no service request. Resolver/audio-persistence structural suites passed 13/13, scoped lint and renderer typecheck pass. Jev `jev-1.14.0` advisory object-identity score: 0.86. No genuine account, generated output, production access, or clean-reload playback was verified; status stays PARTIAL.

- **Re-ticketed from:** ISSUE-1005 (2026-07-21 housecleaning; original status was: `🟡 PARTIAL (2026-07-11 — service/rules path mismatch and destructive cleanup behavior fixed; generation integration/emulator proof remains)`)
- **Status:** 🟡 PARTIAL (2026-07-11 — service/rules path mismatch and destructive cleanup behavior fixed; generation integration/emulator proof remains)
- **Severity:** 🔴 CRITICAL (generated audio cannot become a durable user-library asset)
- **Module:** Audio generation / Audio library persistence
- **Evidence:** `AudioPersistenceService` describes a user-specific audio library and its list/save/delete operations construct `users/${userId}/audio` (`AudioPersistenceService.ts:44-50`, `:67-90`, `:95-117`). The Firestore rules define no `match /users/{userId}/audio/{...}` policy; the only audio-assets rule is for the unrelated root path `/audio_assets/{docId}` (`firestore.rules:1210-1213`), with all unmatched paths denied by the final catch-all (`:1235-1236`). The service’s base constructor itself uses `audio_assets`, but its overridden collection accessor computes the user path and then returns `super.collection` anyway (`AudioPersistenceService.ts:38-42`, `:54-62`), making the declared model contradictory even before any integration adds/reuses base methods.
- **Impact:** Audio metadata read/save/delete requests can fail with `permission-denied`; a generated sound, music, or TTS result may exist only in volatile UI state rather than surviving reload or appearing in its library. Delete can also leave the Storage object untouched when the metadata pre-read is denied.
- **Fix:** Choose one canonical owned-audio document model and make service, rules, storage paths, and client selectors agree. Prefer `users/{uid}/audio/{audioId}` with owner-only schema-validated rules, or use root `audio_assets` consistently with immutable `userId`; remove the misleading override. Await and surface persistence/cleanup outcomes rather than treating an in-memory addition as a saved library asset.
- **Acceptance:** Emulator tests allow an authenticated user to list/create/read/delete only their own generated-audio metadata, reject cross-user access and owner/type/URI spoofing, and cover the exact path the service calls; successful generation survives a clean reload with a playable authorized URL; forced metadata/storage failures retain a retryable pending result with no saved claim; delete either removes both metadata and owned storage object or exposes a durable cleanup-retry state.

- **Fix progress (2026-07-11):** Standardized `AudioPersistenceService` on the already-authorized root `audio_assets` collection, removed the misleading user-subcollection override, added owner-filtered listing, forced authenticated ownership on writes, and changed unauthenticated operations from silent success to explicit failure. Delete now verifies ownership and retains metadata when Storage cleanup fails; `CloudStorageService.deleteAudio()` propagates cleanup failures instead of swallowing them. Added four focused ownership/query/cleanup tests; Vitest, ESLint, renderer TypeScript, and diff checks pass. Remaining before FIXED: connect generated audio creation to awaited metadata persistence with retryable UI state, add emulator coverage for the existing root rules (live edition lookup was unavailable because Firebase credentials require reauthentication), and verify clean-reload playback.

- **Additional progress (2026-07-12):** The audio-library store now has `persistGeneratedAsset()` and `retryAudioPersistence()` rather than only an in-memory `addGeneratedAsset()`: it presents a new result as `pending`, marks it `saved` only after `AudioPersistenceService.saveAudioMetadata()` resolves, and retains a visible `failed` result with an error for retry if persistence rejects. Reloaded library entries are explicitly `saved`. The root `audio_assets` rule now validates owner/document-id consistency, the allowed generation types, bounded duration, required prompt/MIME/timestamp, and requires either a playable storage URL or a bounded data URI; it rejects cross-user and owner/id/type/URI spoofing. Added emulator cases for valid owner create/read, cross-user denial, malformed payload denial, and immutable-owner spoofing. Renderer typecheck and the focused service test pass; Firebase TypeScript build passes. `npm run test:rules --workspace=@indii/firebase` reports 120 passing cases but the harness skips emulator-backed assertions when localhost:8080 is unavailable, so rules behavior still needs a real Emulator run. **Remaining:** repo-wide search confirms there is still no audio generator or UI call site that invokes either persistence action—the new handoff prevents a future generator from falsely claiming save, but does not by itself create a producer. Wire each actual sound/music/TTS completion to `persistGeneratedAsset()` and perform a clean-reload playback test before closing.
- **Production-path progress (2026-07-17):** The real renderer speech producer now calls `generateAudioV3`, and the callable itself owns the durable lifecycle instead of trusting a second client write: idempotent request claim, server cost reservation, supported Gemini 3.1 TTS request, playable WAV wrapping, owner-scoped Storage upload, atomic `creative_jobs` + `audio_assets` completion, reservation settlement/void, failed-commit cleanup, and stored-result replay. Reloaded library reads resolve the `gs://` object to a client playback URL, while delete targets that exact URI and owner Storage rules permit deletion without weakening create/update validation. Focused tests pass. **Still PARTIAL:** only a deployed authenticated Cloud run proving generation, fresh-read playback, idempotent replay, and owner deletion can close ISSUE-1005; local/emulator evidence is explicitly non-acceptance.

The run was blocked, so ISSUE-1691 stays open. I logged that and opened PR [#986](https://github.com/indii-music-founder/indii-music-founder/pull/986), which is ready for review.

**What I saw:** you were signed in on production, and it's running the latest code (build `c1f2c2ae6`, from #984). Distribution shows no releases, and the release form lists no master tracks and no cover art. With no release to name, I never sent the Boardroom prompt, so no AI call was made. That also means there's no Publicist reply, no gateway responses and no console output to report.

**Why it can't pass yet (new ISSUE-1692):**
- **Releases are saved where the Publicist doesn't look.** Distribution keeps releases in one database collection. The playlist-pitch tool only accepts a release from two other collections, and nothing in the app ever creates records there. So a release made in Distribution would be refused with "Forbidden".
- **Web submit is desktop-only.** Submitting a release on the website fails with "Electron environment required". By then it has already saved a half-finished release record.

**In the PR:**

## Summary
No real artist could get a release that the Publicist's MCP tools accept:
- Distribution lists and writes releases in `proprietaryIngestionReleases`.
- `verifyReleaseOwnership` and `generate_playlist_pitch` only read `users/{uid}/releases` and `releases`, and nothing creates documents in either.
- On the web, Submit Release failed inside the Electron-only pipeline after it had already written a partial record.

This blocked the ISSUE-1691 `@live` check (see #986). This branch includes #986's ledger commit; it drops out of the diff if #986 merges first.

**Owner decision:** on the web, Submit Release *saves* the release and leaves delivery to the desktop app.

## Changes
- **`resolveOwnedRelease`** (`packages/firebase/src/mcp/helpers.ts`)
  - Checks `users/{uid}/releases`, then `releases`, then `proprietaryIngestionReleases`. Ownership is by path, or by `userId ?? ownerUid`.
  - Not-found and not-owned return one Forbidden message.
  - Org-shared records owned by another member are refused, because the gateway can't check org membership.
  - `verifyReleaseOwnership` (six tools), the pitch tool and the canvas render job all use it.
- **Pitch grounding:** also reads the nested `metadata` map that Distribution/Publishing records carry. Top-level values win.
- **Canvas render**
  - Reads the master from `assets.audioStoragePath`.
  - **Security:** only downloads objects under the requesting artist's own prefixes. The job uses admin credentials, and the release record is written by the client.
- **Submit Release**
  - Writes the Publishing wizard's `metadata` + `assets` shape via `buildReleaseCatalogRecord`. It stores only canonical storage paths, hashes and fingerprints: no tokenized URLs and no `undefined` values.
  - On the web it runs the server artwork audit, then sets `ready_for_desktop_delivery`. It never calls the pipeline, says no ISRC or UPC was assigned, and labels the button "Save Release".
- **`DistributionSyncService.mapRelease`:** one record without `metadata` used to break the whole catalogue listener. It now reads metadata defensively and falls back to the top-level title and artist.

## Known gap (logged on ISSUE-1692)
The desktop app has no action to deliver an already-saved release. Its Submit creates a new record, so the web copy doesn't promise that delivery can resume this release.

## Test plan
- [x] firebase MCP and canvas suites: 90/90, with new resolver, pitch-grounding, queue-render and path-guard tests.
- [x] renderer Distribution suites: 91/91 (SubmitReleaseModal 14/14, including the web-save and catalogue-shape tests).

# Agent delivery through Entire branches

Coding agents publish locally validated work on task branches through Entire. The repository owner handles remote CI and merging to `main`.

## Solo-owner review policy

All coding agents publish routine changes without GitHub review requests or required human or automated code review. Review is optional when the owner asks for it. Keep local validation and existing CI workflows in place.

1. Push through `origin` with an explicit refspec, such as `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/codex/<task>`. If the user asks for an Entire Trail, use `entire agent-help trail` for the publication and linking commands.

### ISSUE-1693: Dropping an audio file anywhere in the web app always fails ("Failed to save to cloud library")

- **Status:** 🔴 OPEN
- **Severity:** 🟠 HIGH
- **Module:** Global drop zone / StorageService / Hosting CSP
- **Evidence:** production build `8253704d3`, 2026-11-22 ~01:30 UTC, owner account, built-in browser. Dragging `Assembly Line Halo.wav` (WAV, 16-bit/48 kHz, 33.5 MB) onto the page while the Publishing Create Release dialog was open put two entries in the Upload Queue, both "Failed to save to cloud library"; a dropped PNG in the same gesture succeeded. Console: `Connecting to 'data:audio/wav;base64,…' violates the following Content Security Policy directive: "connect-src 'self' blob: …"`, then `[StorageService] Cloud upload failed: TypeError: Failed to fetch` and `[Store] Failed to save item`. Source: `GlobalDropZone.tsx` reads the file with `FileReader` into a `data:` URL (`:168-186`) and calls `addUploadedAudio`; `StorageService` uploads audio/video data URLs with `await (await fetch(item.url)).blob()` (`packages/renderer/src/services/StorageService.ts:225`). `firebase.json`'s CSP `connect-src` has `'self' blob:` but no `data:`, so that fetch is always refused on hosted web. Images take a different branch and succeed.
- **Also observed:** the drop zone's "upload" progress before the read is simulated with `rand()` increments and delays (`GlobalDropZone.tsx:151-166`), so the bar reports progress that is not happening (no-mock-data rule). And a drop over an open dialog goes to the global queue, not the dialog's own file picker.
- **Impact:** an artist cannot add audio to their library by drag-and-drop on the web; the whole file is also held in memory as base64 first (33 MB WAV → ~45 MB string).
- **Fix:** convert the dropped `File` straight to a `Blob` (no `data:` round trip) and upload with `uploadBytes`; or decode the base64 without `fetch` as the image branch does. Do not widen the CSP to `data:`. Replace the simulated progress with real `uploadBytesResumable` progress. Consider letting an open dialog with a file input claim the drop.
- **Acceptance:** on https://indii.music with a genuine account, drop a real WAV: it appears in the library, survives reload and plays; progress reflects bytes sent; no CSP error in the console. Unit test covers the audio branch without `fetch(data:)`.

### ISSUE-1694: A master ingested on the web never reaches the track library, so Submit Release cannot list it

- **Status:** 🔴 OPEN
- **Severity:** 🟠 HIGH
- **Module:** Distribution QC (Pre-Flight Audio & QC) / Track library / Submit Release
- **Evidence:** source on main `8253704d3`. Submit Release lists only masters from `trackLibrary.list()` (`users/{uid}/tracks` with `masterFingerprint` and `masterAsset.audioProperties`; `SubmitReleaseModal.tsx:110-118`), and the live account showed "No canonical masters found — ingest one first" (2026-11-21 run). Distribution's own ingest, the QC tab's web path, uploads the master (`masterAudioService.persist`) and waits for the server analysis receipt (`QCPanel.tsx:228-251`), but never calls `trackLibrary.saveTrack`; no Cloud Function writes `users/{uid}/tracks` from that receipt (only the developer SDK endpoint `sdkTracks.ts:35` creates tracks). On the web, the only UI that saves a canonical master to the library is the Creative video storyboard's audio upload (`StoryboardTimeline.tsx:196`, via `trackIngestion.ingestTrack`).
- **Impact:** an artist who ingests their master in Distribution, the place the Submit Release form tells them to "ingest one first", still cannot select it there. Not yet observed live (needs a successful web upload), so this is a source finding.
- **Fix:** after a successful canonical-master analysis on the web, save the track to the library through the same `trackIngestion` path the storyboard uses (one ingestion service, not a second copy), or point Submit Release's empty state at a path that does.
- **Acceptance:** on production with a genuine account, ingest a WAV in Distribution → Pre-Flight Audio & QC, open Submit Release, and select that master; reload keeps it.

### ISSUE-1695: Publishing catalogue fails with "Missing or insufficient permissions" in the personal workspace

- **Status:** 🔴 OPEN
- **Severity:** 🟡 MEDIUM
- **Module:** Publishing / `useReleases`
- **Evidence:** production build `8253704d3`, 2026-11-22 ~01:30 UTC, owner account on /publishing: console `Error fetching releases: FirebaseError: Missing or insufficient permissions.` (twice). `useReleases(currentOrganizationId)` always queries `proprietaryIngestionReleases` with `where('orgId', '==', orgId)` (`packages/renderer/src/modules/publishing/hooks/useReleases.ts:38-42`). The read rule allows a document only when `userId == auth.uid`, `orgId == auth.uid`, or the caller is a member of `orgId` (`firestore.rules:2398`), so for the personal workspace id `org-default` Firestore cannot prove the query safe and rejects it. `DistributionSyncService.subscribeToReleases` already special-cases `org-default` to query by `userId` for exactly this reason (`DistributionSyncService.ts:58-70`). Which org id the account had was not read from the page, so the `org-default` path is the likely, not confirmed, trigger.
- **Related:** ISSUE-1581 (same `orgId`-only query pattern in `LicensingService`).
- **Impact:** the Publishing catalogue shows "No Releases Found" because the query failed, not because there are none; the error is swallowed into an empty state.
- **Fix:** share one release-query helper between Distribution and Publishing that uses `userId` for the personal workspace and `orgId` for real organizations; surface a load error instead of an empty catalogue.
- **Acceptance:** on production with a genuine personal-workspace account that has a release, Publishing → Catalog lists it with no permission error; an org member sees org releases.
'''

I fixed the upload bug in PR [#991](https://github.com/indii-music-founder/indii-music-founder/pull/991), ready for review. Tests, typecheck and lint pass locally; CI hasn't reported yet, and it isn't on production until you merge and it deploys.

**The bug:** a solo artist has no organization record, so the app keeps a placeholder workspace id (`org-default`) and an empty organizations list. Publishing's Create Release refused every upload and submit unless an organization was loaded, and the error only went to the console. That's why your file picks did nothing.

**What changed:**
- **Uploads:** they only need you to be signed in, since the files are stored under your user id anyway.
- **Saving:** a release saved from your personal workspace is stored as personal, so Distribution lists it as yours. If an organization is selected but not loaded, the form refuses with a clear message.
- **Errors:** any upload failure now shows as a red message in the form.
- **Catalogue:**
  - Publishing now reads your own releases by your user id, which fixes the "Missing or insufficient permissions" error.
  - Older release records missing fields no longer crash the list.
  - If loading fails, it says so instead of showing "No Releases Found".

**Ledger:**
- ISSUE-1695 and ISSUE-1696 are now 🟡 PARTIAL.
- New ISSUE-1697: the chat panel covers the release form, and /publishing leaves the Boardroom on screen.
- New ISSUE-1698: Publishing analytics and payouts also fail with permission errors. I haven't found why.

**Checks:**
- Publishing tests: 58/58, including new cases for your exact situation.
- Typecheck passes.
- Lint is clean apart from one warning that's already on main.
- All of this is mock-based; the real proof is the production run.

**Next:** once #991 is merged and deployed, you pick the WAV and cover in Chrome's Create Release one more time. I take it from there: save the release, confirm it shows in Publishing and Distribution, then run the Publicist pitch.

# Font Consistency Directive

## Goal

Ensure a premium, unified user experience by enforcing the indii typography standard across all application modules.

## Standard Operating Procedure (SOP)

### 1. Single Source of Truth

- All font-family definitions MUST reside in `src/index.css` as CSS variables.
- Standard variables:
  - `--font-main`: Internal/UI Sans (Inter)
  - `--font-mono`: Technical/Code (JetBrains Mono)
  - `--font-display`: Branding/Headers (Geist)

### 2. Tailwind v4 Mapping

- The `@theme` block in `src/index.css` MUST map the following Tailwind utilities:

  ```css
  --font-sans: var(--font-main);
  --font-mono: var(--font-mono);
  --font-display: var(--font-display);
  ```

### 3. Usage Rules

- **Prefer Utilities:** Use `font-sans`, `font-mono`, or `font-display` classes instead of hardcoded font names.
- **Global Default:** The `body` element MUST have `font-family: var(--font-main);` applied via `@layer base`.
- **No Overrides:** Avoid inline `style={{ fontFamily: '...' }}` or local CSS font overrides unless explicitly approved for a specific design-heavy creative module.

## Verification

- Inspect computed styles via browser tools to ensure no fallback to browser defaults (e.g., Times New Roman or user agent sans-serif).
- Verify that dark mode and thematic overrides (like Banana Pro) preserve font consistency.

# indii Design Manifesto: The Resonant Interface (v2026.1)

## 1. Vision & Metaphilosophy
The **indii** interface is a **resonant environment** for creativity, designed for the **2026 Machine Experience (MX)**. We bridge the gap between **Hyper-real AI Perfection** and **Raw Human Authenticity**.

### Core Pillars
*   **Subliminal (MX)**: The UI nudges more than it notifies. It recedes to let the creator's content lead.
*   **Alive (Kinetic)**: Every element breathes, pulses, and reacts. Interaction is a dialogue, not a command.
*   **Artful (Wabi-Sabi)**: We embrace imperfection through subtle noise, organic motion, and "drippy" textures.
*   **Resonant (Sonic)**: Design that you can "hear." Interactions carry potential energy, reinforced by sonic feedback.

---

## 2. The "Drippy" Aesthetic
The signature visual style of indii is the **Drippy 2026 Aesthetic**—a fusion of high-intensity glassmorphism and liquid physics.

### Visual Components
*   **The "Wet Look"**: High-saturation backdrop blurs (`blur-xl`), increased contrast (`saturate-200`), and ultra-thin translucent borders.
*   **Liquid Borders**: Dynamic, pseudo-element borders that feel like they are flowing or "dripping" around containers.
*   **Spotlight Interaction**: Surfaces react to the cursor with radial gradients (`glowColor`) that follow movement, creating a sense of depth and focus.
*   **Noise & Grain**: A persistent, low-opacity noise overlay (`opacity-[0.04]`) adds tactile depth and counters AI sterility.
*   **Scanlines**: Subtle technical overlays (`opacity-[0.03]`) signal the platform's high-fidelity processing nature.

---

## 3. Design Tokens (The Frequency Theme)

### A. Color Palette
| Token | Hex | Usage |
| :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Void** | `#030303` | Primary background; deepest OLED black. |
| **Resonance Blue** | `#2E2EFE` | Primary action; electric, digital energy. |
| **Frequency Pink** | `#FE2E9A` | Accent; creative life-force and highlights. |
| **Dopamine Pink** | `#FF0099` | Secondary accent; high-saturation optimism. |
| **Electric Blue** | `#00F0FF` | Technical highlights and data flow. |
| **Signal White** | `#F0F0F0` | Primary typography; high contrast, low harshness. |

### B. Gradients
*   **Tech Bro**: `Resonance Blue` to `Electric Blue` (The SaaS/AI standard).
*   **Dopamine**: `Dopamine Pink` to `Frequency Pink` (Creative energy).
*   **Liquid Chrome**: Multistop silver/white gradients for high-impact headlines.

### C. Typography
*   **Primary (Sans)**: `Geist Sans` (Technical but human, highly legible).
*   **Technical (Mono)**: `Geist Mono` (For metadata, IDs, and code-like elements).
*   **Hierarchy**: Oversized headlines (tracking-tighter) paired with tiny, wide-tracked uppercase secondary text (`tracking-[0.4em]`).

---

## 4. Interactive Architecture

### The Spotlight Card System
The primary container for all content. It must include:
1.  **Primary Glow**: Cursor-following radial gradient.
2.  **Secondary Blur**: Larger, softer secondary glow for "atmosphere."
3.  **Internal Sheen**: Gradient-to-tr from `white/0.02` to transparent.
4.  **Drippy Border**: High-intensity border with slight hover elevation (`hover:-translate-y-2`).

### Kinetic Motion (Framer Motion)
*   **No Abrupt Appearances**: Everything must fade, scale, or slide with high-damping springs (`stiffness: 100, damping: 20`).
*   **Capability Ticker**: Horizontal scrolling "data-streams" of keywords to signal operational supremacy.
*   **Scanline Pulses**: Step-based animations that mimic data flow across visual elements.

---

## 5. Implementation Directives

1.  **No Ad-Hoc CSS**: All styling must use Tailwind utility tokens or the centralized `index.css` system.
2.  **Mobile Perfection**: The landing experience must be "iPhone-Perfect," respecting touch targets and viewport constraints.
3.  **Accessibility as Default**: Minimum AA contrast, focus indicators, and support for "Reduced Motion" OS preferences.
4.  **Intent-Based Navigation**: Use "Agentic UX" patterns—Dialogue-based navigation ("Get me in") over traditional action buttons.

---

## 6. Sonic OS Identity
The UI is the visual representation of the **indii Sonic DNA**.
*   **Audio Visualizers**: Real-time 4K synthesis of audio into visual manifests.
*   **Sonic Feedback**: Buttons "click," panels "whoosh," and the system "hums" with potential energy.

---

## 7. Production Integrity & Specialized Components
While aesthetics are "drippy" and "resonant," the interface must remain functionally ironclad.

### A. Safety Patterns
*   **ConfirmDialog**: All destructive actions (Delete, Remove, Cancel) must utilize the `ConfirmDialog` component. It uses the Radix `Dialog` primitive but follows the indii aesthetic (glassmorphism + loading states).
*   **Data Loss Prevention**: The `useConfirmDialog` hook is the mandatory pattern for stateful confirmation flows.

### B. Compliance UI
*   **CookieConsentBanner**: GDPR-compliant, transparent tracking management. It must integrate with the "Resonant" theme—clear, non-intrusive, yet authoritative.
*   **Privacy Layers**: Interfaces involving sensitive data should use the "Fog" effect (high blur) when not in active focus.

---

## 8. Technical Implementation (CSS Utilities)
To maintain consistency, use the following pre-defined utility classes in `globals.css`:

### Class Definitions
*   `.glass-panel`: Implements the "Wet" look with `backdrop-filter: blur(30px) saturate(200%)` and subtle internal shadows.
*   `.drippy-border`: Uses a pseudo-element mask to create a high-fidelity, light-reactive edge without standard border limitations.
*   `.text-chrome`: Applies the `liquid-chrome` gradient to text, mimicking polished metal.
*   `.glow-text-[blue|pink]`: Applies multi-layered text shadows for a "neon-on-black" resonance effect.
*   `.animate-liquid`: A 15s ease-infinite background drift for gradient-heavy surfaces.
*   `.perspective-2000` & `.transform-style-3d`: Core utilities for creating high-depth layouts.

### Atmosphere Layer
The system uses a global **Grainy Texture Layer** (`body::after`) with `mix-blend-mode: overlay` at `0.05` opacity to create a physical, tactile surface across the entire viewport.

> **Directive**: If it looks static, add a pulse. If it looks dry, add a drip. If it looks silent, add a hum. If it's destructive, add a check. If it's code, make it mono.

## 2024-05-22 - Accessible Icon Buttons in Collapsed Navigation

**Learning:** Collapsed sidebars often rely on visual cues (icons) but strip away text labels, leaving screen reader users without context unless `aria-label` is explicitly managed based on the collapsed state.
**Action:** When implementing collapsible navigation or UI elements, always pair the visual state toggle with a corresponding `aria-label` update or ensure the tooltip/accessible name is robust enough to handle the text-less state.

## 2024-05-23 - Exposing Hidden Accessibility Features

**Learning:** Powerful accessibility features (like voice input) often exist in the codebase logic (e.g., `handleMicClick`) but are inaccessible because they lack a UI trigger, assuming they are "nice to haves" or "future features".
**Action:** Actively audit service layers for capabilities (like `VoiceService`) that are not exposed in the UI and create explicit, accessible triggers (buttons with `aria-label`) for them, especially for alternate input methods.

## 2024-05-23 - Resurfacing Hidden Accessibility Features

**Learning:** Found critical voice accessibility logic (`handleMicClick`) buried in unused code. Features that aid accessibility (like dictation) should not be hidden behind arbitrary flags or missing UI, as they benefit all users, not just those with disabilities.
**Action:** When auditing components, check for "dead" event handlers that might be orphan accessibility features. Re-enable them with proper visual states (`isListening`) and feedback loops.

## 2024-05-24 - Semantics of Custom Loaders

**Learning:** Custom loading components often lack semantic meaning, relying purely on visual cues like spinners. Adding `role="status"` and `aria-live="polite"` makes them immediately accessible to screen readers without changing the visual design.
**Action:** Always wrap custom loaders in a container with `role="status"` and ensuring inner decorative elements (spinners) are hidden with `aria-hidden="true"`.

## 2025-02-20 - Nested Interactive Elements Conflict

**Learning:** In the `LayersPanel`, the parent `div` had `role="button"` and an `onKeyDown` handler for selection, which inadvertently intercepted `Enter` key events from nested action buttons (visibility, lock, etc.), breaking their keyboard accessibility.
**Action:** Added a check in the parent's `onKeyDown` handler to ignore events originating from nested `BUTTON` elements, ensuring that child actions remain accessible while preserving row selection.

## 2025-05-24 - File Input Accessibility

**Learning:** File inputs hidden with `display: none` (or `.hidden`) inside labels cannot be focused via keyboard, breaking accessibility for uploaders.
**Action:** Use `.sr-only` on the input to keep it in the DOM/accessibility tree, and apply `focus-within:ring` to the parent label to provide visual focus indication.

## 2025-05-24 - Semantic Loading States

**Learning:** Custom visual loaders like `DeptLoader` often rely purely on visual cues (spinners), leaving screen reader users unaware of processing states.
**Action:** Always wrap custom loaders in `role="status"` with `aria-live="polite"` and include visually hidden text (or `aria-label`) if no visible text is present.

## 2024-05-24 - Segmented Controls as Tabs

**Learning:** Segmented controls that switch between distinct views are often implemented as buttons, missing the semantic relationship between the control and the view. Using `role="tablist"`/`tab`/`tabpanel` clarifies this relationship for screen readers.
**Action:** When a set of buttons toggles exclusive views, upgrade them to the ARIA Tab pattern to provide context on the current selection and the controlled content.

I restyled the Create Release dialog in PR [#993](https://github.com/indii-music-founder/indii-music-founder/pull/993), ready for review. I haven't seen it rendered, because that needs a deploy.

**What was wrong:**
- **Oversized content:** the box itself was the intended width. The content inside it was too big: large headings, tall inputs, big upload areas, a 48px icon and a 128px cover thumbnail. The Assets step ended up scrolling inside a small area.
- **Clipped step bar:** the six-step bar was cut off at "Revie…".
- **Off-style:** it used generic blue and gray, unlike the other Studio dialogs.

**What I changed (only `ReleaseWizard.tsx`):**
- **Same look as Submit Release:** near-black panel, thin white borders, small uppercase labels, compact inputs, white primary buttons.
- **Publishing's own green:** it replaces blue and green wherever one marks the active step, a finished step or a selected option, so it matches the rest of Publishing.
- **Smaller everything:** upload areas, icons and the cover thumbnail are much smaller.
- **Step bar:** it now fits inside the dialog.
- **Unchanged:** behavior, and the upload and error fixes from #991.

**Checks:**
- Publishing tests: 54/54.

content.text:
Yes, a few are the right size, and most of the rest aren't. I only compared the class names in the code, so none of this is confirmed by looking at the screen.

I used the Submit Release dialog as the reference. It has a `text-lg` title, `max-w-xl`, and no oversized padding. I scanned all 99 files that use a full-screen overlay (`fixed inset-0`) and ranked them by large headings (`text-2xl` and up) and `p-8` to `p-12` padding.

**Probably the right size**
- `SubmitReleaseModal`: the reference.
- `AddEntityModal` in the project canvas: no large headings and no oversized padding.
- `InstrumentApprovalModal`.
- `ErrorBoundary`: only one large heading.

**Likely oversized, worst first**
- `DropCampaignWizard` (Merchandise): four `text-2xl`, many `p-8` and larger.
- `CampaignDetailsModal` (Publicist): `text-3xl` and `text-2xl` headings.
- `ReleaseKitModal` (Publicist): `text-2xl`, `p-8`, and a `max-w-4xl` box.
- `DaySheetModal` (Touring): `p-8` and `p-10`, plus `text-2xl`.
- `ConnectDistributorModal` (Distribution): `text-2xl` and `p-8` in a `max-w-lg` box. This is the closest match to the Create Release problem.
- `ExpenseManualEntryModal` (Finance): `text-xl` and `p-8` in a `max-w-md` box.
- `FreeMiniCampaignModal` (Creative) and `PreSaveCampaignBuilder` (Marketing): `text-2xl` and `p-8`.
- `AccountCreationWizard` (Social): `text-2xl` and `p-8`.

**Probably full pages, not pop-ups:** `PublicistDashboard`, `SelectOrg`, `KnowledgeBase`, `OnboardingPage`, `FileDashboard`. Big text is likely intended there.

Do you want me to restyle the oversized ones to match Submit Release? I'd start with `ConnectDistributorModal`, `ExpenseManualEntryModal`, `CampaignDetailsModal` and `DropCampaignWizard`. I'd do them as a separate PR from #993.
Yes to all
